newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: SOCCER-CHILAVERT, ASPRILLA OFF AS PARAGUAY BEAT COLOMBIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT, ASPRILLA OFF AS PARAGUAY BEAT COLOMBIA.

text.p: Paraguay goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert and Colombia's Faustino Asprilla, two of the world's top players, were sent off as Paraguay beat Colombia 2-1 in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
The two were dismissed for fighting in an incident which led to a brawl on the pitch involving the players, both team benches and riot police. Play was held up for nearly five minutes.
During the melee, Colombian striker Victor Aristizabal, who had just been substituted, was seen lashing out while captain Carlos Valderrama had to be restrained by teammates after losing his temper.
The Colombian players appeared incensed at the behaviour of the Paraguayan police. Aristizabal was also shown the red card.
Chilavert and Asprilla fell out as they went for the ball following a cross.
The incident, in the 81st minute, led to a penalty which was converted by Mauricio Serna to wipe out a lead Paraguay had held from the early stages.
But in a dramatic finale, Derlis Soto slid in Paraguay's winner less than two minutes later.
The win put Paraguay three points ahead of Colombia at the top of the single South American group.
With four of their seven remaining games at home, where they have a perfect record, Paraguay now look certain to qualify for the World Cup for the fourth time and the first since 1986.
Colombia, unbeaten until they lost at home to Argentina in their previous game, are still four points ahead of third-placed Bolivia.
Both teams will rue the minimum one-match suspension which awaits their star players.
Paraguay captain Chilavert, an explosive, charismatic figure whose mere presence seems to intimidate opponents, has lifted and inspired his team after ending a self-imposed national team exile.
His unusual ability to score from free kicks and penalties has earned him fame worldwide.

Asprilla has scored six goals for Colombia, who were missing key players Freddy Rincon, Wilmer Cabrera and Jorge Bermudez through suspension, in the tournament although he has not hit the target in the last four games.
Paraguay, backed as usual by a fanatical 40,000-strong crowd, took an early lead when defender Carlos Gamarra scored at the far post following a free kick on the left.

Colombia, less physical and more technical, dominated for spells in an intriguing, evenly balanced game and created several chances before equalising. The best fell to Asprilla, whose effort was blocked by an advancing Chilavert.

Paraguay - 1-Jose Luis Chilavert, 3-Catalino Rivarola, 5- Celso Ayala, 4-Carlos Gamarra, 2-Francisco Arce, 15-Harles Bourdier, 10-Roberto Acuna, 20-Julio Enciso, 16-Derlis Soto, 18- Aristides Rojas, 19-Julio Yegros (21-Pedro Sarabia, 67).

Colombia - 1-Farid Mondragon, 13-Jose Santa, 15-Osmar Lopez, 3-Alexis Mendoza, 4-Hugo Galeano, 8-Harold Lozano, 6-Mauricio Serna, 14-Leonel Alvarez (7-Antony de Avila, 89), 10-Carlos Valderrama, 9-Victor Aristizabal (17-Richard Hamilton, 75), 11- Faustino Asprilla.
